cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Rome, and he calls them brothers. He's just spent chapters explaining how God saves people, and it ended with him breaking into praise. Now he turns it all toward everyday life, starting with one big word: Therefore.

cards.question: Paul says, "Therefore I urge you, brothers," and he gives the reason he's urging them. On account of what?

cards.text: Then Paul reaches for a word from the old altar: sacrifice. But what he asks them to offer is not what you'd expect, friend.

cards.question: What does Paul urge the believers in Rome to offer to God as a sacrifice?

cards.text: Their bodies, offered as "living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God" in Paul's words. A sacrifice that wakes up, hits snooze, and is STILL a sacrifice.

cards.question: Paul says offering your body as a living sacrifice is your spiritual service of worship.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Do not be conformed to this world," and friend, I'm a cookie stamper. Pressing dough into my shape was my WHOLE job, so trust me when I say: don't let this world be your stamper.

cards.question: Instead of being conformed to this world, Paul says to be transformed. How?

answers.text: By the renewing of their mind
By the keeping of the law
By the strength of their will

cards.question: Paul says once their minds are renewed, they'll be able to test and approve something good, pleasing and perfect. What is it?

cards.text: Next, Paul has a word for every one of the believers in Rome. It starts with how they see themselves.

cards.question: What does Paul tell every one of the believers in Rome not to do?

cards.text: Instead, Paul says to think of yourself with sober judgment. I used to think I was the finest stamper in that kitchen, and then a shiny new one showed up, and sober judgment arrived the SAME DAY.

cards.question: Paul says to measure yourself by comparing yourself to the people around you.

cards.text: Paul says the measure is the faith God has given each one. Then he points to something everyone carries around: one body with many parts, and not every part does the same job.

cards.question: Using the picture of the human body, what does Paul say the many believers in Christ are?
Paul says each member of the body of believers belongs only to himself.

cards.text: Each member belongs to one another. Picture a foot deciding to go solo, friend, and I hop around on a gold base, so trust me, that foot is going NOWHERE.
Different parts, different jobs, and Paul says the believers have different gifts too.

cards.question: Paul writes that believers have different gifts according to the ___ given them.

cards.text: Then Paul runs a list: if your gift is prophecy, use it in proportion to your faith, and if it's serving, serve, and if it's teaching, teach. No meeting about the meeting, friend, just TEACH.
If your gift is encouraging, encourage. Then Paul starts adding not just what to do, but how to do it.

cards.question: If a believer's gift is giving, how does Paul say to give?
Paul says the believer whose gift is leading should lead with diligence.
If a believer's gift is showing mercy, Paul says to do it ___.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage without references: that Paul is an apostle of Christ Jesus (Romans 1:1), that he writes to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:7), and that the earlier chapters end with him breaking into praise (Romans 11:33-36). The card cites only Romans 12:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Saying what Paul asks them to offer "is not what you'd expect" rules out "Their best lambs" on card 4, because lambs are the expected altar sacrifice.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Four of the stop's five choice cards are multiple choice, there is one true or false, and there is no fill in the blank. One type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "It starts with how they see themselves" points straight to the right answer on card 2. It rules out "Speak up before they pray", which has nothing to do with how they see themselves.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Speak up before they pray" is not the same kind of thing as the other two answers, which are about how people view or trust themselves.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to the backstory: that he thought he was the finest stamper in the kitchen until the new one arrived. This also conflicts with the backstory, which says he was already worn down and his stamps were blurry before the new stamper came.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This true or false tests a made-up idea (measuring yourself by comparison) instead of what the text gives as the measure, which is the faith God has given (Romans 12:3). That measure is only told afterward, on card 5. The joke on card 3 just before it shows Papa Dorin getting sober judgment by comparing himself to the new stamper, which points the baker toward True.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The question says "Using the picture of the human body," which gives away "One body" and rules out "One vine" and "One flock" without any reasoning.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke blends two images that don't connect: a foot going solo, and Papa Dorin hopping on his gold base. It's unclear why his base means the foot goes nowhere, so a stranger would say "huh?".

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The card retells "Different parts, different jobs" from Romans 12:4 but cites only Romans 12:6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Then Paul starts adding not just what to do, but how to do it" isn't true. Paul already added a how in Romans 12:6, telling the one with the gift of prophecy to use it in proportion to his faith.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.
